clue.text: The picture appears masterly framed by a Greek character

indicators.note: framed by says the word for masterly sits inside the Greek letter, as a picture sits in a frame

parts.note: tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
masterly means skilful or able

explanation.surface: Someone admires a painting that looks as if a great master did it, set inside an ornamental Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed by' is the container signal; 'masterly' is not about painting but simply means able. 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or arranged group, a living picture, from the French for a painting.

clue.text: Try this concoction when wanting a drink

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of try this are mixed up

explanation.surface: A barman offers a new cocktail to a customer who wants a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' sounds like the drink on offer but signals mixing the letters of TRY THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty describes feeling the need for liquid, so a thirsty person is in want of something to drink.

clue.text: The worker's holding one's taken back say to invest

indicators.note: holding says the bee's letters surround the other two pieces

parts.note: a worker bee is the typical worker of the hive

indicators.note: taken back says the letters for one's are read in reverse order

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I plus S
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A worker is holding on to something reclaimed in order to put money into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns only one's into SI; 'holding' wraps BEE round it plus EG. 'invest' is not about money: in the old military sense it means surround a town with troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town, in the military sense, is to surround it with troops, which is to lay siege to it.

clue.text: Polish fellows gripped by a newspaper leader

indicators.note: gripped by says the word for fellows is held inside the editor's letters

parts.note: the editor heads a newspaper, abbreviated ED
fellows means men

explanation.surface: Polish men are grabbed by the editor of a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb polish, as in refine a text, not the nationality; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, which is to polish it.

clue.text: Cast off clothing

parts.note: read as old discarded garments, but it describes someone who has thrown off what they were wearing

explanation.definitionFit: To be undressed is to be naked or partly unclothed, having removed one's garments.

clue.text: Rough and ready way to score

explanation.surface: A crude method of putting points on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch team or meal is thrown together roughly; to score a surface is to mark it with a sharp line, as a scratch does.

clue.text: Walk under a quarter, being diminutive

indicators.note: under in a down clue says the walk is placed below the quarter

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a mall is a sheltered walk or promenade, as in The Mall in London

explanation.surface: A small figure walks beneath a district of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts MALL below S; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminutive means very small in size.

clue.text: Restore control on political power

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keep a tight rein
the state is the political power governing a country

explanation.surface: A politician promises to restore control over government.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places REIN above STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put back in a former place or condition, which is to restore.

clue.text: Labour has got a number in tow

indicators.note: in says a and the number go inside the word for tow

parts.note: to trail something is to drag or tow it behind
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The Labour Party has gained a following that it pulls along behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has got' is a link; 'in' puts A and V inside TRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or arduous work, an old word for toil and also for childbirth.

clue.text: Weapon of the mob — about a pound in weight

indicators.note: about says the word for the mob goes round the other letters

parts.note: a herd is a crowd or mob of people
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A rioter's weapon weighing about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, not a rough guide to the weight; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a combined spear and battleaxe on a long pole, a medieval weapon.

clue.text: Rather stained material

indicators.note: material here is stuff to be worked into something else, so the letters of stained are raw material to be remade

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric that prefers to be stained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a noun for cloth beside 'stained', but it signals that the letters of STAINED are to be reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead and rather both mean in place of something else, as in tea rather than coffee.

clue.text: A great bother for a woman

parts.note: great means big
to ail is to trouble or bother someone

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a woman is a great nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, from a character in a 17th-century play, so the clue can call her simply a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a female name and, in older English, a lady's maid.

clue.text: Rate a water supply essential to raise such a plant

parts.note: rate as in the rate of travel means speed
a well is a source of water dug into the ground

explanation.surface: A gardener says a steady supply of water is vital for growing this flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence about watering; 'essential to raise' is linking material leading to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant of the genus Veronica, common in British gardens and verges.

clue.text: Measure a little plate

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a small piece of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale is a graded system for measuring; it is also a thin flake or plate, like those on a fish.

clue.text: Admit defeat and return

explanation.surface: Someone gives in and goes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give in; a yield is also the return on an investment or the crop a field produces.

clue.text: Decision-making course

explanation.surface: A route that has to be chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction is the management or guidance of affairs; it is also the course or way something travels.

clue.text: Shown design fault, set about everyone

indicators.note: set about says the scrambled letters are placed round the word for everyone
a fault means the letters of design are not in their proper order and must be rearranged

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A design flaw was revealed and announced to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' makes SIGNED from the six letters, and 'set about' splits it round the word for everyone. 'Shown' is the past participle, matching the answer's -ed ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To have signalled something is to have indicated or displayed it, so it has been shown.

clue.text: The guard reading order out in front of the queen

indicators.note: in front of says the scrambled piece comes before the queen's letters
order out says the letters of reading are taken out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A palace sentry reads out an order in front of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order out' makes GRENADI from the seven letters; 'in front of' sets it before the Queen's cipher. The Grenadier Guards are a regiment that guards British royal palaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of the Grenadier Guards, a British regiment of foot guards.

clue.text: Down town there's a bar with game

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: In a town down the road there is a pub that offers a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' is County Down in Northern Ireland, not a direction; BANBRIDGE is a town there. 'bar' suggests a pub but is the verb ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Banbridge is a market town in County Down, Northern Ireland, so it is a town in that county.

clue.text: Note swine going around in top gear

indicators.note: going around says the word for swine encloses the musical note

parts.note: boars are wild or male pigs, that is, swine
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Pigs circling a note while dressed in their best clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' means headgear, not a car's highest gear: boaters are flat-topped straw hats. 'going around' is the container signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Boaters are stiff straw hats with flat crowns, a type of headwear worn on top.

clue.text: A fertiliser can put up value

indicators.note: put up in a down clue says the word for can is written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
rate means to value or assess

explanation.surface: A farmer finds that a tin of fertiliser goes up in price.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put up' turns TIN to NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates, salts of nitric acid, are widely used as fertilisers, so a nitrate is one such.

clue.text: Cancel the right to go in peace

indicators.note: to go in says the letter for right is put inside the word for peace

parts.note: ease is a state of peace and rest

explanation.surface: An order cancels someone's right to enter in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go in' puts R inside EASE; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, which cancels whatever was written.

clue.text: Trouble — a barrier is required to contain it

indicators.note: to contain says the barrier's letters surround the word it

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: To keep trouble in, a fence is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' is the container signal; 'it' is used as it stands, and 'is required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to disturb or stir up, which is to trouble.

clue.text: A high spot for the first mate and others

parts.note: in the Bible Eve was Adam's wife, the first woman and so the first mate
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A ship's officer and crew climb to a high place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first mate' suggests a ship's officer, but it is Eve, the first wife; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, so it is literally a high spot.

clue.text: Like sound detective in old Mexico

indicators.note: sound says the word for like is to be taken as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: like as in just like means as
tec is a short informal word for a detective

explanation.surface: A private eye working in old Mexico who sounds the part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' changes the word for like into the letters that say the same, AZ. The Aztecs ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people of the empire in Mexico before the Spanish conquest, so an Aztec is one found there long ago.

clue.text: Turn work into play

parts.note: read as a call to stop working and have fun, but it means adapting a written work, such as a novel, for the stage

explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise a story is to adapt it as a stage or screen drama.

clue.text: Benefactor presenting college authority with gold

parts.note: a don is a senior teacher at an Oxford or Cambridge college
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A benefactor gives a college academic some gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presenting' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives, as a benefactor does.

clue.text: Gives support to dreadful beast

indicators.note: dreadful says the letters of beast are in a terrible state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone backs a horrible animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' signals rearranging BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or assist, usually in wrongdoing, so abets means helps along.

clue.text: Joy is a member of the family but no leader

indicators.note: but no leader says the word for a family member loses its first letter

parts.note: a relation is a member of one's family

explanation.surface: Happiness is a family member, except for the head of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no leader' drops the R from the start of RELATION; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: Repeat a trite broadcast with some point

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered seed means the letters of a trite are spread about and rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: A radio station reruns a hackneyed programme that still has some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns A TRITE into ITERAT, and E (east, a compass point) completes it; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, the root of reiterate.

clue.text: More backward? Well more inflexible anyway

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for being more behind than ever and even more rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: The stern is the back of a ship, so the first sense is a nautical joke: further astern.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern is the rear of a ship, so sterner jokingly means further back; stern also means strict and unbending.

clue.text: Particular courtesy

explanation.surface: Being polite in a fussy way.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a particular point or detail, as in in every respect; respect is also politeness and regard.
